newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore prompt diesel prices slumps-traders.
newsitem.headline: Singapore prompt diesel prices slumps-traders.

text.p: Singapore prompt diesel slumped on Tuesday to $22.90 per barrel, down $1.40 from the last trade done last week, traders said.
Traders said they estimated the price was the lowest in a year and would add further pressure to already depleted refinery margins.
Traders said British Petroleum Co Plc sold 150,000-barrel cargo to Japanese trader Marubeni International Petroleum Co, part of Marubeni Corp, for lifting ex Singapore June 25-29.
Gas oil prices have been falling sharply after three major buyers slowed down their buying support for the market and after China's buying appetite disappeared.
In addition, product prices have been pressured lower by a slump in crude prices during the past week by almost 10 percent.
Traders said they expected prices to remain soft for some weeks.
Some support could then emerge on buying ahead of the winter and from Indonesia to cover for refinery maintenance shut downs.
